title: The uncomfortable: what to do when it surfaces

outline.heading: The thing that makes practice do anything at all
What showed up once somebody finally asked

points.text: Britton, Lindahl, Cooper, Canby and Palitsky (Clinical Psychological Science, 2021) — 96 participants in an eight-week programme.
Goldberg, Lam, Britton and Davidson (Psychotherapy Research, 2022) — a US population sample, 434 people with meditation experience:
And one detail from there that is rarely retold: people who reported harm were just as glad they had practised as everyone else.
The review by Matko and Van Dam (Current Opinion in Psychology, 2026) summarises the spread: 25–87% of practitioners report adverse effects, 3–37% report functional impairment.
Unpleasant effects are common, and persistent harm is rare — on the order of a few per cent up to the mid-teens.

outline.heading: Where to go if it persists beyond the session

points.text: If the heaviness reaches past the session and holds for several days, ease off practice and contact a living professional.
